---
title: "Image formats (R)"
format:
  html:
    code-tools: true
filters:
  - panzoom
panzoom:
  hint: false
---

Two figures, a wide collage and a standard plot, written by different knitr
graphics devices: webp, svg, png, and pdf. Every figure has the
`#| panzoom: true` cell option and opens in panzoom unless its case says
otherwise. How figures of other shapes open is on [wide and tall
figures](h-wide-and-tall-r.html).

knitr has no built-in webp device, so the webp cases use `agg_webp` from ragg.
knitr passes it sizes in inches and no resolution, while ragg expects pixels and
draws at 72 dpi, so each webp case sets both under `dev.args`:

```yaml
#| dev.args:
#|   units: "in"
#|   res: 96
```

`res: 96` gives the webp the same size as the page's other figures.

The collage cases draw with this helper:

```{r}
library(ragg)

# A collage: `n` panels side by side, like a wide patchwork figure.
collage <- function(n = 12) {
  set.seed(1)
  par(mfrow = c(1, n), mar = c(3, 3, 2, 1))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    plot(
      cumsum(rnorm(200)),
      type = "l",
      main = paste("Panel", i),
      xlab = "",
      ylab = "",
      col = hcl.colors(n)[i],
      lwd = 2
    )
  }
}
```

## webp collage {expect-fit="height"}

A 25 × 2 inch collage written as webp. It opens in panzoom at screen height.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| dev: agg_webp
#| dev.args:
#|   units: "in"
#|   res: 96
#| fig-ext: webp
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   A row of 12 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color
#| fig-cap: "A 25 × 2 inch collage of 12 random walks."

collage(n = 12)
```

## svg collage {expect-fit="height"}

The same collage written as svg. It opens in panzoom at screen height.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| dev: svg
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   A row of 12 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color
#| fig-cap: "A 25 × 2 inch collage of 12 random walks."

collage(n = 12)
```

## webp plot {expect-fit="contain" shift-scroll="none" expect-scale="1"}

A small plot written as webp. It opens in panzoom at its real size.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: agg_webp
#| dev.args:
#|   units: "in"
#|   res: 96
#| fig-ext: webp
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Filled contour map of Maunga Whau's heights in terrain colors, with a color
#|   key
#| fig-cap: "Maunga Whau's heights as filled contours."

filled.contour(volcano, color.palette = terrain.colors)
```

## svg plot {expect-fit="contain" expect-scale="1"}

The same plot written as svg. It opens in panzoom at its real size.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: svg
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Filled contour map of Maunga Whau's heights in terrain colors, with a color
#|   key
#| fig-cap: "Maunga Whau's heights as filled contours."

filled.contour(volcano, color.palette = terrain.colors)
```

## png and pdf {expect-fit="contain"}

A plot written as both png and pdf. The page shows the png, which opens in
panzoom.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: [png, pdf]
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Filled contour map of Maunga Whau's heights in terrain colors, with a color
#|   key
#| fig-cap: "Maunga Whau's heights as filled contours."

filled.contour(volcano, color.palette = terrain.colors)
```

## png and cairo_pdf {expect-fit="contain"}

Case 5 with the cairo PDF device, which embeds fonts and handles Unicode (µ,
Greek letters) and transparency better than `pdf`. The page shows the png, which
opens in panzoom. With a PDF device alone, there is no image to open. Quarto
embeds the PDF in a small box with the browser's PDF viewer, which panzoom
leaves alone.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: [png, cairo_pdf]
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Filled contour map of Maunga Whau's heights in terrain colors, with a color
#|   key, titled mu = 5, alpha = 0.05
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Maunga Whau's heights as filled contours, titled mu = 5, alpha = 0.05, as
#|   png (and cairo_pdf).

filled.contour(
  volcano,
  color.palette = terrain.colors,
  plot.title = title(main = "mu = 5, alpha = 0.05")
)
```

## webp past its size limit

A 100 × 5 inch collage as webp at 192 dpi. At 19,200 px wide it is past the webp
limit of 16,383 px per side, so ragg can't write the file. The page shows a
broken image, and clicking it opens the viewer with "The image could not be
loaded." in place of the image.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| error: true
#| fig-width: 100
#| fig-height: 5
#| dev: agg_webp
#| dev.args:
#|   units: "in"
#|   res: 192
#| fig-ext: webp
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   A row of 12 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color
#| fig-cap: "A 100 × 5 inch collage of 12 random walks."

collage(n = 12)
```

## Animation {expect-open="panzoom" expect-fit="contain"}

One cell with `fig-show: animate` and twelve plots, which knitr joins into one
animated gif with the gifski package (`animation.hook: gifski`). It opens in
panzoom and keeps playing while it zooms and pans.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-show: animate
#| animation.hook: gifski
#| interval: 0.2
#| fig-alt: "A sine curve sliding to the right over one period, frame by frame"
#| fig-cap: "A sine wave, y = sin(x - t), as t runs over one period."

x <- seq(0, 4 * pi, length.out = 400)
for (t in seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 13)[-13]) {
  plot(x, sin(x - t), type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#3B7DB8", ylab = "sin(x - t)")
}
```
